name: TOF10120 laser distance sensor (I2C)
description: Laser (940 nm, class 1) time-of-flight distance sensor: 100–1800 mm indoors on a white target, about ±5 %, a new reading every ≤33 ms. Runs on 3–5 V, 35 mA. Has both a UART (9600 8-N-1, ASCII commands such as r6#) and an I2C port; this part uses I2C at address 0x52 (datasheet ID 0xA4 in 8-bit form): write register 0x00, read 2 bytes = distance in mm, high byte first. Sold as: TOF10120 laser range sensor module 10-180 cm UART/I2C with 6-wire cable (GND, VDD, RXD, TXD, SDA, SCL).
eli5: Shines an invisible laser blip and times how long it takes to bounce back, then tells your board the distance in millimetres.

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Supply 3–5 V, 35 mA (pin 2). Use 3.3 V on ESP32 / Pico so the TTL serial pins stay at 3.3 V

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: UART input, 9600 baud TTL (pin 3): ASCII commands like s3-1# or s7-164#. Not needed for I2C use

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: UART output, 9600 baud TTL (pin 4): ASCII replies / distance stream. Not needed for I2C use

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (pin 5); add a 4.7 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (pin 6); add a 4.7 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V

supplierQuery: TOF10120 laser range sensor module UART I2C
buildNotes: I2C address 0x52 (the datasheet writes it as 0xA4, the 8-bit write address). Write register 0x00, wait at least 30 µs, read 2 bytes: distance mm = byte0 × 256 + byte1.
The module measures continuously; readings are the filtered distance by default. Send s3-1# over its UART for the real-time distance instead.
Reliable range is about 100–1800 mm on a white target indoors (80 cm on grey, less in sunlight). Values outside that range are not trustworthy.
Power it from 3.3 V on an ESP32 or Pico; its serial pins are TTL at the supply level. Fit 4.7 kΩ pull-ups on SDA and SCL to 3.3 V.
The connector is a tiny 1.0 mm 6-pin socket: use the supplied cable. Wire colours vary between batches, so follow the pin order GND, VDD, RXD, TXD, SDA, SCL printed on the board.
Keep the cover glass clean; smudges cause cross-talk and short readings.

driver.code:
# TOF10120 laser time-of-flight distance sensor (Sharp SPAD ranging module), MicroPython driver, I2C side.
# Datasheet (Shenzhen Hongchengji TOF10120): VDD 3-5 V, 35 mA, range 100-1800 mm, ranging time max 33 ms,
# I2C slave ID 0xA4 by default (8-bit form; 7-bit address 0x52), changeable over UART with "s7-xxx#".
# Reading (vendor example code): write the register pointer 0x00, wait >= 30 us, then read 2 bytes:
#   distance in mm = high byte * 256 + low byte.
# Whether that value is the filtered or the real-time distance is set by the UART command "s3-x#"
# (x=0 filtered, the default; x=1 real-time).
import time

ADDR = 0x52  # 0xA4 >> 1


class TOF10120:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=ADDR):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr

    def distance_mm(self):
        """Latest distance in millimetres (the module measures continuously, about every 30 ms)."""
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'\x00')
        time.sleep_ms(1)  # vendor code: at least 30 us between pointer write and read
        d = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 2)
        return (d[0] << 8) | d[1]

    def distance_cm(self):
        return self.distance_mm() / 10

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from tof10120 import TOF10120

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
sensor = TOF10120(i2c)
while True:
    print('D=%dmm' % sensor.distance_mm())
    time.sleep_ms(500)
